$comment: HayesX-250 preflight checklist, transcribed from Flight Manual HayesX-250-FM-001 Rev A, Chapter 4. Item text is verbatim from the manual except where 'normalised' is true. This file is the single source of truth for the app's checklist; the app must render it, never hard-code items.

rules.validityNote: Proposed, not from the manual. See docs/06-open-questions.md Q3.

sections.title: Preflight Preparation
sections.intro: The pilot shall verify the following. These are legal declarations by the pilot in command.

items.text: He/she is physically fit for flight
Is not under the influence of alcohol or drugs

items.ref: FM 2.7 — VMC only. Prohibited: cloud, dense fog, heavy rain, thunderstorm, known icing.

items.text: It is permissible to fly in the proposed area
items.ref: FM 2.7 — no-fly zones, restricted areas, danger areas, TFRs, congested areas.
FM 2.5 — minimum 95% before takeoff; verified numerically at J-05.

items.text: Ensure cantilever arms secure and rigid at joints
All critical fasteners marked with red torque-seal paint are secure and show no signs of loosening, fracture, or misalignment
Make sure they are securely attached
Check propeller tie wire fixing is intact
Check all marked joints show no evidence of movement or misalignment
Check to ensure no excessive play
Ensure there are no foreign objects
Check to ensure no bulge in the battery

warningBefore.text: Once activated, parachute deployment cannot be cancelled. The GBS 10M parachute has a 6-year validity period. This rescue system is a pyrotechnic device and must be disassembled or repaired by authorised personnel only.

items.unresolvedNote: The source document carries an unanswered author query: 'Question for Ben — should the safety pin be removed before flight?' Do not ship this item until HayesX confirms the intended state. See docs/06-open-questions.md Q1.

items.ref: FM 2.6 — activation handle is on the pilot's left side.

sections.title: Power-Up Procedure
sections.intro: HayesX-250 uses a dual 108 V DC electrical power system. The front and rear battery packs connect to the main power system through QS12 high-voltage connectors. High-voltage system maintenance shall only be performed by trained personnel.

warningBefore.text:
DO NOT connect or disconnect QS12 connectors under electrical load.
DO NOT short-circuit battery terminals.
DO NOT operate with damaged connectors.

subsections.title: High-Voltage Connector Inspection
subsections.orderNote: The manual prints this inspection after the connection sequence, but it must be performed before connecting. Ordered inspection-first here — confirm with HayesX. See docs/06-open-questions.md Q2.

items.text: QS12 connectors undamaged and in good condition
Locking mechanism is normal and functional

subsections.title: Main Power Connection
subsections.sequentialNote: Steps must be confirmed one at a time in this order. The order is the safety property.

items.text: Confirm both main power connectors are disconnected
Connect Front Battery QS12 Main Power Connector
Connect Rear Battery QS12 Main Power Connector

abnormalConditions.trigger: Available as a persistent action from this section onward.
abnormalConditions.action: Disconnect power immediately and discontinue operation.

sections.title: System Initialisation
sections.intro: After both battery systems are connected, the Flight Control System powers up automatically.

sections.title: Propulsion System Check
sections.intro: Inspect all eight propulsion arm control modules.

items.text: Eight green status indicators illuminated continuously

sections.title: Boarding Procedure
sections.intro: All pilot operations and movements must be within the Formula 1 inspired roll cage. No arm movements are permitted outside the roll cage (FM 4.1).

items.text: Ensure aircraft is stable and secure before boarding

items.failText: Battery charge is below the 95% minimum required before takeoff.
items.ref: FM 4.7 and FM 2.5 — Minimum Battery Before Takeoff 95%.

limitsReference.$comment: Surfaced in-app next to the relevant checks and in the Manuals tab. Sourced from Flight Manual Chapter 2.
